fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says the son of the Israelite woman "…blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:11) A fight had broken out in the camp between him and an Israelite. After that, they brought him to Moses, Israel's leader.

The text doesn't mention any stealing, friend. A fight breaks out in the camp, and then the son of the Israelite woman "…blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:10-11) Nothing is said about a tent or anything taken from it. The serious thing he does is with his words.

Running off isn't what the text says, friend. It says a fight broke out in the camp, and the son of the Israelite woman "…blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:10-11) Then they brought him to Moses, Israel's leader. The serious thing he does is curse the Name.

The text doesn't say that, baker. It says, "They placed him in custody…" (Leviticus 24:12) The passage names his mother, Shelomith daughter of Dibri, but it never says he was given to anyone in his family. He's held until the will of the LORD is made clear.
Yes, friend. They hold him "…until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) The waiting is for the LORD's will. Then the LORD speaks to Moses. (Leviticus 24:13)

Not quite, baker. The LORD says, "…the whole assembly must surely stone him, whether he is a foreign resident or native…" (Leviticus 24:16) So the law covers the foreign resident as well as the native. Neither one is left out.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "Whoever kills an animal must make restitution…" (Leviticus 24:18) So restitution is the answer for an animal. Then He says, "…whoever kills a man must be put to death." (Leviticus 24:21) Two different cases, and two different outcomes.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 24:22) That's the reason the text gives. It's stated right there in the same verse as the command.
